task: Resolve the data consistency issue after the sharding migration changed the partition key.

candidate_memories.content: Reads from shard 3 return stale data because the routing layer still uses the old customer_id-based partition key.
After the migration, the routing layer must use tenant_id as the partition key for all shard lookups.
The sharding migration completed on March 15; any data written before that date may still be on old shards.
When a partition key changes, update routing before any new writes to prevent reads from returning stale shards.
Shard 3 is the only affected shard; shards 1, 2, and 4 were migrated and verified before the routing issue appeared.
The database sharding was originally designed for a 4-shard topology; the migration expanded it to 8.
Session 5 note: the data team ran a quarterly reconciliation that found no discrepancies.
Old lesson: consistent hashing with virtual nodes was considered but rejected for this sharding design.
The analytics pipeline reads from a separate read replica and is not affected by the sharding key change.
The infrastructure team deployed new EC2 instances for shard 4 in session 18.
Old routing note: customer_id was chosen as the partition key for locality with the billing system.
After any partition key change, run a full consistency check across all shards before opening traffic.
Session 9 note: the search team indexed the customer table for name-based lookup.
The sharding library used is vitess with custom routing rules configured in the shard map.
A load test in session 14 confirmed all shards handle 1000 queries/second without saturation.
The backup schedule was updated to include shard-level snapshots after the migration.
Old practice: routing layers used a static shard map before dynamic discovery was added.
Session 7 note: the data team created a new dashboard for shard health monitoring.
Tenant IDs are UUIDs assigned at account creation; customer IDs are sequential integers.
Old migration guide: the original sharding key change was planned for Q4 but was moved to Q1.
